title: regional-margin-repo-hc-tradebook
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures a small-batch scenario analysis for regional margin reallocation ("repo" = reassigning reserved capacity and budget between regions during a 90d sprint), and the headcount tradebook tied to pricing velocity changes. Intended as the Finance + Product short-form playbook for a leadership decision on whether to: (A) shift reserved capacity to lower-cost regions and hire fewer infra ops headcount, or (B) hold regionally matched capacity for SLA reasons and absorb higher unit cost by adjusting route pricing.

Notes / background context (quick):
- We observed 18% YoY growth in hosted token volume from NA and 24% YoY in EMEA. APAC requests are growing but still <12% of spend. (source: billing export, cleaned)
- GPU pricing differentials: US-west spot-equivalent ~1.0x baseline, EU-west reserved premium +7%, APAC on-demand premium +20% (current provider quotes).
- SLA requirement: some enterprise customers require at least 1 region local capacity; shifting too much capacity out of region may trigger escalations and credits.
- This doc focuses on a reallocation window: 90d active repo + 6mo headcount phasing implications.

Key assumptions (editable cells in sheet):
- baseline-avg-price-per-token: $0.00035
- unit-inference-cost (US baseline): $0.00022/token (includes amortized GPU, infra, networking)
- EU uplift factor: 1.07; APAC uplift factor: 1.20
- reserved-capacity-shiftable: 60% of flexible pool without violating SLA triggers
- hire-lag-for-infra-ops: 8 weeks per hire on average (from req-to-productive)
- HC cost fully-loaded: $220k/year per senior infra engineer (including benefits, taxes, bench)

Scenario matrix (summary table; rows = scenarios):
Scenario,Description,Avg price/token,Unit cost/token,Gross margin,HC delta (FTE over 6mo),Budget delta ($k over 6mo)
Base (status-quo),No region shift,$0.00035,$0.00022,37.1%,0,$0
Repo-to-EU-Majority,Shift flexible pool to EU (60%) with slightly higher unit cost,$0.00035,$0.00024,31.4%,-1,$-165
Repo-to-APAC-Beta,Shift 40% to APAC (cheaper reserved deals in APAC negotiated),$0.00033,$0.00020,39.4%,+0,$+120
Hold-Local-Premium,Keep capacity local to meet SLAs,raise price 5% on affected routes,$0.000368,$0.00024,34.8%,+2,$+320
Aggressive-Quantize,Combine regional shift + model quantization (saves 12% unit cost),$0.00034,$0.00019,44.1%,-1,$-210

Notes on table calculations:
- Gross margin = (price - unit cost) / price. Budget delta assumes 6 months of run-rate for token consumption of the affected pool (~2.5B tokens over 6 months for the flexible pool), and HC delta converts to 6-months of fully-loaded cost.

Sensitivity slices (what moves the needle):
1) Spot vs reserved price curves: A 10% worse spot price increases unit cost by ~0.015 cents/token and can flip Repo-to-APAC from net positive to marginal.
2) Volume haircuts: If flexible pool volume dips >20% (seasonal churn), the marginal benefit of region shifts drops as amortization for reserved capacity increases.
3) SLA penalty regime: Any customer upgrade in the enterprise cohort that requires local-only capacity triggers a 50–80% reduction in shiftable capacity.

Mini-capacity schedule (operational levers):
- Week 0–2: Legal review of SLA language for reassigning reserved capacity (owner: Legal, ticket JIRA-FIN-782)
- Week 2–6: Procurement renegotiate APAC reserved blocks (owner: Procurement)
- Week 3–10: Infra ops hiring (2 hires conditional) + onboarding calendar (owner: Eng-Infra)
- Week 8–12: Execute controlled traffic shift (canary 5% -> 25% -> 60%) with rollback windows after each step (owner: SRE)

Headcount tradebook (6mo horizon):
- Option A (shift heavy to lower-cost regions): reduce 1 infra headcount (senior) by delaying backfill, reassign 0.5 SRE to procurement coordination for 6 months. Net FTE delta: -1.0 senior equivalent over 6 months.
- Option B (protect local capacity): accelerate 2 hires (SRE + infra), increase short-term contractor spend. Net FTE delta: +2.0 over 6 months.
- Option C (mix + tech savings): hold hires but invest $120k in quantization/compilers to reduce unit cost; HC delta: 0 net but Opex reallocation.

Risk checklist (short):
- Contractual risk: check customers with locality clauses (action: Legal review, due week 2).
- Operational risk: can we sustain cold-start latency from cross-region routing? SRE to run 72h latency spike test.
- Reputational risk: enterprise accounts flagged for potential credit; CS to prepare customer comms template.
- Accounting: reserved move may change CAPEX/OPEx treatment; FP&A to confirm treatment (linked Confluence).

Quick sensitivity scenarios (cell-friendly paste for the sheet):
"""
scenario,price_adj_pct,unit_cost_adj_pct,expected_tokens_m,notes
base,0,0,2500000000,Status quo
apac_promo,-5,-12,2500000000,apac reserved promo reduces unit cost
eu_shift,0,9,2500000000,slightly higher unit cost but cheaper infra headcount impact
hold_local,5,9,2500000000,raise price to protect margin while keeping local capacity
quantize,-2,-12,2500000000,apply quantization savings
"""

Actionable next-steps (owner tags):
- @Procurement (Priya Shah): get binding 90d option quotes for APAC/EU by 2026-11-22.
- @Legal (Liam O'Connor): surface all locality clauses and produce a short red/amber/green list by 2026-11-09.
- @SRE (Ethan Zhou): run cross-region latency spike test and canary plan draft by 2026-11-16.
- @FP&A (Marina Alvarez): model 6-mo cashflow P&L for the four scenarios and attach a one-pager with break-even headcount points. Due 2026-11-19.

Open questions (to resolve in next meeting):
- Is there appetite from sales to accept a small price delta (3–5%) for enterprise customers in lieu of promise of local capacity? (Sales input required)
- What fraction of flexible pool is truly non-contractual for each major account? Need CS account-level mapping.
- Could we accelerate quantization roadmap to unlock 8–12% cost savings inside the 90d window? (Eng research ask)

Notes-to-self / rough heuristics: 
- If unit-cost differential (regional) > 0.00003/token and shiftable volume > 1.5B tokens, prioritize repo unless legal blocks.
- Hiring lag means headcount decisions have asymmetric timing vs price-change windows; prefer option mixes that decouple immediate price moves and hires (e.g., APAC reserved leases + contractor overlay).

Meeting cadence / approvals:
- Weekly check-in (finance + procurement + eng-ops) for 6 weeks.
- Final go/no-go decision to exec sponsorship if expected 6mo delta > $250k.
